title: Krishna Directs Arjuna to Hymn Durga
one_line_summary: On the eve of the battle Krishna tells Arjuna to recite his hymn to Durga; the goddess appears in the sky, grants victory, and both warriors blow their conches.

primary_source.work: Mahabharata (Kisari Mohan Ganguli English translation, all 18 parvas)

source_excerpt: The holy one said,--'Cleansing thyself, O mighty-armed one, utter on the eve of the battle thy hymn to Durga for (compassing) the defeat of the foe.' ... Understanding (the measure of) Partha's devotion, Durga who is always graciously inclined towards mankind, appeared in the firmament and in the presence of Govinda, said these words. The goddess said,--'Within a short time thou shalt conquer thy foes, O Pandava. O invincible one, thou hast Narayana (again) for aiding thee.'
notes: Pre-battle frame to the Bhagavad Gita in the Ganguli edition (the 'hymn to Durga' is an appendix/khila).

title: Krishna Places the Chariot Between the Armies
one_line_summary: At Arjuna's request Krishna drives the chariot between the two assembled armies so Arjuna can survey the kinsmen he must fight.

primary_source.work: Mahabharata (Kisari Mohan Ganguli English translation, all 18 parvas)

source_excerpt: Arjuna said,--'O thou that knoweth no deterioration, place my car (once) between the two armies, so that I may observe these that stand here desirous of battle...' Sanjaya continued,--'Thus addressed by Gudakesa, O Bharata, Hrishikesa, placing that excellent car between the two armies, in view of Bhishma and Drona and all the kings of the earth, said,--'Behold, O Partha these assembled Kurus.'

title: Arjuna's Despair and Collapse
one_line_summary: Seeing his kinsmen arrayed on both sides, Arjuna is overcome with pity, his bow Gandiva slips from his hand, and he casts aside his weapons and sinks down on his chariot.

primary_source.work: Mahabharata (Kisari Mohan Ganguli English translation, all 18 parvas)

source_excerpt: Beholding all those kinsmen standing (there), the son of Kunti, possessed by excessive pity, despondingly said... 'My body trembles, and my hair stands on end. Gandiva slips from my hand, and my skin burns... I wish not to slay these though they slay me, O slayer of Madhu...' Having spoken thus on the field of battle, Arjuna, his mind troubled with grief, casting aside his bow and arrows, sat down on his car.
notes: Bhagavad Gita chapter I (Vishada Yoga / 'Survey of Forces').

title: Arjuna Surrenders to Krishna as Disciple
one_line_summary: Unable to see his duty, Arjuna lays down his arms in spirit and begs Krishna to instruct him as his disciple.

primary_source.work: Mahabharata (Kisari Mohan Ganguli English translation, all 18 parvas)

source_excerpt: Arjuna said,--'...My nature affected by the taint of compassion, my mind unsettled about (my) duty, I ask thee. Tell me what is assuredly good (for me). I am thy disciple. O, instruct me, I seek thy aid.'
notes: Bhagavad Gita chapter II; the moment of surrender that opens Krishna's teaching.

title: Krishna Grants Celestial Sight and Reveals the Vishvarupa
one_line_summary: At Arjuna's request, Krishna gives him divine sight and reveals his supreme universal form filling the heavens.

primary_source.work: Mahabharata (Kisari Mohan Ganguli English translation, all 18 parvas)

source_excerpt: Arjuna said,--'...I desire to behold thy sovereign form. If, O Lord, thou thinkest that I am competent to behold that (form), then... show me thy eternal Self.' The Holy One said,--'...Thou art, however, not competent to behold me with this eye of thine. I give thee celestial sight. Behold my sovereign mystic nature.' Sanjaya continued,--'Having said this... Hari, the mighty Lord of mystic power, then revealed to the son of Pritha his Supreme sovereign form, with many mouths and eyes, many wonderous aspects...'

title: Krishna Declares 'I Am Death'
one_line_summary: Within the cosmic form Arjuna sees the warriors rushing into Krishna's flaming mouths, and Krishna reveals himself as all-consuming Time commanding Arjuna to be his instrument.

primary_source.work: Mahabharata (Kisari Mohan Ganguli English translation, all 18 parvas)

source_excerpt: Arjuna said,--'...all these sons of Dhritarashtra... are quickly entering thy terrible mouths rendered fierce by thy tusks. Some, with their heads crushed, are seen striking at the interstices of (thy) teeth...' The Holy One said, 'I am Death, the destroyer of the worlds, fully developed. I am now engaged in slaying the race of men... By me have all these been already slain. Be only (my) instrument.'

title: Krishna Returns to His Gentle Form
one_line_summary: Terrified and repentant, Arjuna begs Krishna to resume his familiar form; Krishna comforts him and restores him to his senses.

primary_source.work: Mahabharata (Kisari Mohan Ganguli English translation, all 18 parvas)

source_excerpt: Arjuna said,--'...Beholding (thy) form (unseen) before, I have been joyful, (yet) my mind hath been troubled, with fear. Show me that (other ordinary) form, O God...' Sanjaya continued,--'Vasudeva, having said all this to Arjuna, once more showed (him) his own (ordinary) form, and that High-Souled one, assuming once more (his) gentle form, comforted him who had been afflicted.' Arjuna said,--'Beholding this gentle human form of thine, O Janardana, I have now become of right mind and have come to my normal state.'

title: Arjuna Resolves to Fight
one_line_summary: His delusion dispelled, Arjuna declares he will do Krishna's bidding and returns to battle.

primary_source.work: Mahabharata (Kisari Mohan Ganguli English translation, all 18 parvas)

source_excerpt: Arjuna said, 'My delusion hath been destroyed, and the recollection (of what I am) hath been gained by me, O Undeteriorating one, through thy favour. I am now firm. My doubts have been dispelled. I will do thy bidding.'
notes: Bhagavad Gita chapter XVIII; the return to battle that closes the Gita.

title: Krishna's Overture to Karna
one_line_summary: After the Gita, Krishna approaches Karna and invites him to fight for the Pandavas until Bhishma falls, but Karna refuses out of loyalty to Duryodhana.

primary_source.work: Mahabharata (Kisari Mohan Ganguli English translation, all 18 parvas)

source_excerpt: Vasudeva then went to Radha's son on the field of battle. And the elder brother of Gada, for the sake of the Pandavas, then said to Karna,--'It hath been heard by me, O Karna, that from hatred of Bhishma thou wilt not fight. Come to our side, O son of Radha, and (stay with us) as long as Bhishma is not slain...' Karna said, 'I will not do anything that is disagreeable to Dhritarashtra's son, O Kesava. Devoted to Duryodhana's good, know that I have cast off my life (for him).'

title: Krishna Counsels Arjuna to Let Karna Pass
one_line_summary: Krishna holds Arjuna back from fighting Karna, warning that Karna still holds the infallible dart that Vasava (Indra) gave him.

primary_source.work: Mahabharata (Kisari Mohan Ganguli English translation, all 18 parvas)

source_excerpt: Thus addressed by Savyasachin, the mighty-armed Kesava, endued with great energy, replied in these opportune words, 'The mighty-armed Satyaki is singly a match for Karna, O son of Pandu!... For the present, O Partha, it is not proper for thee to fight with Karna. The latter hath with him the blazing dart, like a fierce meteor, that Vasava gave him. O slayer of hostile heroes, he hath kept it for thy sake, worshipping it with reverence... I know, O son of Kunti, this wicked wight's hour, when, indeed, thou wilt, with keen shafts, throw him down from his car.'

title: Krishna Lends His Car to Satyaki
one_line_summary: Krishna foresees Satyaki's need, summons his charioteer Daruka by blowing his conch, and lends his own celestial car to Satyaki for the fight with Karna.

primary_source.work: Mahabharata (Kisari Mohan Ganguli English translation, all 18 parvas)

source_excerpt: Before even the encounter, Krishna knew it in his heart that the heroic Satyaki would be vanquished... Janardana, O king, knoweth both the past and the future. For this, summoning his charioteer, Daruka, he had commanded him, saying, 'Let my car be kept equipped tomorrow.' ... With Kesava's permission, upon that car guided by Daruka, and which resembled the blazing fire or the sun in effulgence, ascended the grandson of Sini.

title: Krishna Embraces and Praises Arjuna After the Vow
one_line_summary: When Arjuna's vow against Jayadratha is fulfilled, Krishna embraces him, and Arjuna credits the victory entirely to Krishna's grace.

primary_source.work: Mahabharata (Kisari Mohan Ganguli English translation, all 18 parvas)

source_excerpt: At that frightful time when confusion was everywhere... Hrishikesa, stationed in the van of battle embracing Arjuna who had accomplished his vow, told him these words, 'By good luck, O Jishnu, thy great vow hath been accomplished...' Unto him Arjuna replied, 'Through thy grace, O Madhava, this vow that even the gods could with difficulty accomplish, hath been accomplished by me... This is thy victory, O lord!'

title: Krishna Shows Arjuna the Slain Battlefield
one_line_summary: As they ride back across the field, Krishna points out to Arjuna the fallen kings, elephants, and horses slain by his shafts.

primary_source.work: Mahabharata (Kisari Mohan Ganguli English translation, all 18 parvas)

source_excerpt: Then Krishna said, 'Desirous of victory in battle or world-wide fame many heroic kings are lying on the earth, struck with thy shafts... Behold, O hero, those huge creatures afflicted with shafts lying on the ground in convulsions... This fame-enhancing and mighty feat on the field of battle is capable of being achieved by thee only, O puissant one...'

title: Krishna Rallies the Broken Pandava Host
one_line_summary: Seeing the Panchalas routed by Drona and Karna, Krishna urges Arjuna to cast away fear and advance against the two great warriors.

primary_source.work: Mahabharata (Kisari Mohan Ganguli English translation, all 18 parvas)

source_excerpt: Seeing the Panchalas slaughtered and routed, Janardana becoming cheerless, said these words unto Phalguna, '...Beholding the host fly away, through fear, ye Pandava warriors, cast away your fears! Accompanied by all the forces and arraying then, in good order, both of us, with uplifted weapons, are even now proceeding against Drona and the Suta's son for withstanding them.'

title: Krishna Sends Ghatotkacha Against Karna
one_line_summary: Krishna keeps Arjuna from Karna and instead commands the Rakshasa Ghatotkacha to fight Karna at night, so that Karna's infallible dart is spent on him.

primary_source.work: Mahabharata (Kisari Mohan Ganguli English translation, all 18 parvas)

source_excerpt: Vasudeva said, 'I behold Karna, O son of Kunti... I do not, however, O sinless one, regard the time to have come, O mighty-armed one, for thee to encounter the Suta's son in battle. The blazing dart... given him by Vasava, is still with him... Let the mighty Ghatotkacha proceed against the son of Radha.' ... Then he of Dasarha's race, addressed Hidimva's son... 'Slay Karna in battle, at this dead of night, aided by thy illusions.'
notes: The pivotal stratagem: Ghatotkacha is sent to force Karna to waste the Vasava dart.

title: Krishna Directs Ghatotkacha to Slay Alayudha
one_line_summary: When Bhima is hard-pressed by the Rakshasa Alayudha, Krishna tells Ghatotkacha to abandon Karna for the moment and first slay Alayudha.

primary_source.work: Mahabharata (Kisari Mohan Ganguli English translation, all 18 parvas)

source_excerpt: Vasudeva, approaching Ghatotkacha, said unto him these words, 'Behold, O mighty-armed one, Bhima is violently assailed by the Rakshasa in battle... Abandoning Karna for the present, quickly slay Alayudha, O mighty armed one! Thou can afterwards slay Karna.' Hearing these words of him of Vrishni's race, the valiant Ghatotkacha, abandoning Karna, encountered Alayudha...

title: Krishna Rejoices at Ghatotkacha's Fall
one_line_summary: While the Pandavas mourn Ghatotkacha, Krishna dances and shouts for joy, then reveals the cause: Karna's infallible dart is now spent and Karna is mortal.

primary_source.work: Mahabharata (Kisari Mohan Ganguli English translation, all 18 parvas)

source_excerpt: Only Vasudeva filled with transports of delight, began to utter leonine shouts, grieving the Pandavas... Tying the steeds and uttering loud roars, he began to dance in a transport of joy, like a tree shaken by a tempest... Vasudeva said, 'Great is the joy I feel. Listen to me, Dhananjaya!... know, O Dhananjaya, that Karna, his dart being baffled through Ghatotkacha, is already slain in battle.'
notes: Krishna's apparent cruelty at Ghatotkacha's death is explained as strategic relief.

title: Krishna Recounts His Slaying of Enemy Kings
one_line_summary: Krishna explains to Arjuna that, for the Pandavas' good, he contrived the deaths of Jarasandha, Ekalavya, Sisupala and Ghatotkacha himself.

primary_source.work: Mahabharata (Kisari Mohan Ganguli English translation, all 18 parvas)

source_excerpt: Vasudeva said, 'If Jarasandha, and the ruler of the Chedis, and the mighty son of the Nishada king, had not been slain, they would have become terrible... For thy good, the Nishada's son also... was, by an act of guile, deprived of his thumb by Drona... For thy good, he was slain by me on the field of battle. Endued with great prowess, the ruler of the Chedis was slain by me before thy eyes.'
notes: Retrospective on Krishna's role in removing the Pandavas' foes.

title: Krishna Explains His Protection of Arjuna
one_line_summary: Krishna tells Satyaki how he always shielded Arjuna from Karna's dart, stupefying Karna so the weapon was never hurled at Partha.

primary_source.work: Mahabharata (Kisari Mohan Ganguli English translation, all 18 parvas)

source_excerpt: Vasudeva said, '...I, however, O foremost of warriors, always used to stupefy the son of Radha. It was for this that he did not hurl the dart at Pandu's son... I do not regard my sire, my mother, yourselves, my brothers, ay, my very life, so worthy of protection as Vibhatsu in battle... Beholding Dhananjaya, therefore, like one returned from the dead, these transports of delight, O Yuyudhana, have been mine.'
notes: Contained within the file section_181.txt under the heading 'SECTION CLXXXII' (section 182 is not a separate file in the bundle). | [citation: SECTION CLXXXII heading sits inside corpus file section_181; cited as 181]

title: Krishna Consoles the Grieving Yudhishthira
one_line_summary: When Yudhishthira is overwhelmed by grief at Ghatotkacha's death, Krishna urges him to rise and fight rather than sink into despondency.

primary_source.work: Mahabharata (Kisari Mohan Ganguli English translation, all 18 parvas)

source_excerpt: Beholding him so afflicted, Krishna said these words, 'O son of Kunti, let not such grief be thine. Such cheerlessness does not become thee, O chief of the Bharatas, as it does an ordinary person. Rise, O king, and fight. Bear the heavy burden, O lord! If cheerlessness overtakes thee, our victory becomes uncertain.'

title: Krishna Devises the Ashvatthama Stratagem
one_line_summary: Seeing Drona unbeatable in battle, Krishna counsels the Pandavas to abandon fair means and tell Drona that his son Ashvatthama is slain, so he will lay down his arms.

primary_source.work: Mahabharata (Kisari Mohan Ganguli English translation, all 18 parvas)

source_excerpt: Kesava, endued with great intelligence and devoted to their welfare, addressed Arjuna and said, 'This foremost of all bowmen is incapable of being ever vanquished by force in battle, by the very gods with Vasava at their head. When, however, he lays aside his weapons, he becomes capable of being slain on the field even by human beings. Casting aside virtue, ye sons of Pandu, adopt now some contrivance for gaining the victory... Upon the fall of (his son) Aswatthaman he will cease to fight, I think. Let some man, therefore, tell him that Aswatthaman hath been slain in battle.'
notes: The origin of the 'Ashvatthama hath been slain' deception.

title: Krishna Urges Yudhishthira to Speak the Untruth
one_line_summary: As Drona is about to annihilate the Pandava army, Krishna presses the truth-loving Yudhishthira to tell the half-truth that Ashvatthama is dead.

primary_source.work: Mahabharata (Kisari Mohan Ganguli English translation, all 18 parvas)

source_excerpt: Meanwhile, O monarch, Govinda, knowing that Drona... was capable of sweeping all the Pandavas off the face of the earth, became much distressed. Addressing Yudhishthira he said, 'If Drona fighteth, filled with rage, for even half-a-day, I tell thee truly, thy army will then be annihilated. Save us, then, from Drona. Under such circumstances, falsehood is better than truth. By telling an untruth for saving a life, one is not touched by sin. There is no sin in untruth spoken unto women, or in marriages, or for saving a king, or for rescuing a Brahmana.'
notes: Krishna's justification of the 'white lie' that causes Drona to lay down his arms.
